findings.reason: the plan must either extend the flight declaration to omit `CLAUDE.md` and read its harness home, or state why a second live-settings hook carrier cannot drift from reckon's.
findings.text: with `--setting-sources ''` the plan's profile route reads the `hooks` block from the operator's live `~/.claude/settings.json` (`USER_SETTINGS="${CLIVE_USER_SETTINGS:-${HOME}/.claude/settings.json}"`, line 773) and merges it into the `--settings` file (lines 862, 898-902); this is a second implementation of the harness-home hook carry that reckon already owns and declares, in `reckon/schema/flight-defaults.yaml:42-43` (`path: settings.json`, `keys: [hooks]`) implemented at `reckon/_backends.py:2141-2144` and `reckon/_backends.py:2288`. The two carriers diverge: under the fence `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is the run's harness home, but clive reads `${HOME}/.claude/settings.json`, so the hooks the worker actually runs are the operator's mutable live set, not the per-run set the fence computed and shipped — the plan's own §2 text first adopts that declaration (snapshot line 54) and then abandons it (line 56) in favour of the live read.

findings.reason: the section must state, in its own text, what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be, before it adds this surface.
findings.text: §2 adds to three of the four families and accounts for none: a new `--worker-profile PATH` CLI option on clive (cli_options), a new three-key public profile file contract plus the `$CLIVE_PROFILE_RECEIPT` env variable (public_definitions), and a named-refusal vocabulary for a missing file, a malformed key, a missing path and an empty `tools` list (refusal_families) — the section text names nothing it retires or merges, and gives no reason retirement is impossible.

findings.reason: the plan's own value-add (per-file sha256, empty-`--setting-sources` route, receipt) is behaviour a plain flag list cannot supply, so the wrapper is justified even though the hook carry is not.
findings.text: the profile expands to flags Claude Code already accepts, and the plan rejects a generated `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` but does not weigh extending reckon's existing settings carry (named under duplicate_owner) as the alternative to a new launcher flag layer.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the single `--worker-profile PATH` interface hides validation, file digesting, hook-merge, route selection and the receipt behind one flag and one reused settings/argv path, which is depth rather than a spread of wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan re-implements the hook-carry path that reckon's flight declaration already owns.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §2 adds a CLI option (`--worker-profile`), a three-key profile file and a named-refusal vocabulary without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan cites the mechanisms it threads through rather than adding a parallel launcher: clive's existing `--settings`/`--append-system-prompt` argv builder in `imas_ambix/agent/clive.py` and reckon's harness-home flight declaration; the only same-package "profile" loader, `imas_ambix/agent/profile.py`, is model-serving configuration and a genuinely different domain, so it is not reuse the plan missed.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the plan adds `--worker-profile` as a layer over Claude Code's own `--settings`/`--mcp-config`/`--append-system-prompt` flags, and although it justifies the flag route against a generated `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, it never says why the profile's hook-carry cannot instead extend the existing owner of "which hooks a worker runs under".
